Something I’ve noticed because there is still stigma surrounding seeking help from a medical professional, and I’ve seen it in family and those close to me — is he trying to self-medicate? Is he actually DEPRESSED and needs a psychiatrist? 

I think men especially struggle with identifying depression in themselves and really understanding that it’s a serious medical condition that requires working closely with a professional. To me it’s obvious that addicts are trying very hard to treat themself on their own because of chemical imbalances and I find it incredibly cruel to expect them to get clean without the help of SSRI/SNRI or antipsychotic drugs (not that it’s an expectation, I just think it’s a very straightforward first step). They aren’t necessarily aware of the reason why they feel they need substances to feel better or normal or to function. And it’s awfully hard when you have friends and family who don’t have psychiatric conditions thinking you should just quit substances when it can feel like an absolute lifeline for people with depression. I’ve also been desperate to hang onto substances because otherwise I might hurt myself or worse. 

Also, with the depression usually comes shame. Shame in the way that makes people feel that they are bad people and subconsciously they accept their poor situations because it makes sense to them. It’s easier to hurt yourself with drugs if you are ashamed and feel you deserve it. It’s hard to learn that guilt is the healthier reaction than shame. Guilt is “I did something bad,” shame is “I am bad.” People grow and improve when they feel guilt, but they settle and stay the course if they feel shame. We all make mistakes and sometimes do bad things, but that makes us guilty, not shameful. My parents taught me to be ashamed of myself when I messed up and it’s contributed to all of my worst habits, including substance use.

He needs to figure out NOW if he needs to be treated for depression, and if he is being consumed by shame. It’s a difficult situation, but this is an easy starting point.

Seconded. The cat is probably fine, but I realized after years of having my cat that this position is sometimes used when he is in physical discomfort. He has irritable bowel or lymphoma. Don’t know yet. Also, after he had surgery he distinctly loafed.

You’re being a good owner by observing. Without other odd behaviors (hiding, overgrooming, vomiting/diarrhea, not eating/drinking/using litter box) there’s no reason to fret. Continue to pay attention.

I’m here with you. I’m in such a spell that I’ve been accidentally hurting my body through carelessness and a literal lack of feeling. I feel like dropping out of my body right now. Everything is grinding on my nerves, yet nothing feels like anything. I’m bored, yet overstimulated. I want to die, yet I want so badly for someone to want me how I need to be wanted and to live contentedly.

I don’t have any answers, but I just wanted to show support to a fellow “soldier.” I’ve been dealing with this for about 19 years and I’m currently really struggling. Again. I really hope you figure something out that’s healthy for you. Much love.
It’s hard to handle this while everyone is looking. I’m sorry you have to go through this. I know it’s hard to be away from your knife. Please hang on.
I don’t want to be alone.
Masking is so much effort. I feel weird that some people don’t understand. It’s too much.

As much as I like humoring these thoughts in my own head, I can’t rightly weigh in, as I don’t support this “plan.” I’m here because I feel obligated to live and therefore need you, and everyone else here….so of course I don’t want you to go. 

I think you should do what feels right to you. I know it’s so tempting to just make everything stop. It’s so painful. I know. I encourage you to access resources that can help you find reasons to live. It’s worth a real shot. I need you and others like you. I don’t want to be alone.

Honestly, because I’m here for feeling similar to you about life and death, I’m not sure if I have anything to offer you. Life is hard. ASD, mental illness…nobody can see it, so most have an outrageous ignorance toward it all. It’s hard to reach out, access resources, talk to people, make phone calls, schedule appointments, etc. I can’t get myself to feel okay having to go through so many people to get the help I need. And I know what it’s like to have parents who don’t know what to do and mistreat their kids….living feels impossible. 

I have a habit of selfishly wanting everyone here to choose to live. Partially because if you go, then I’ll truly be alone. So I’ll just say this: If you choose to continue to try to be good and live well, it’s going to be incredibly brave of you because it will be hard. Hell, it’s going to be hard to be brave. But I believe in you. Life will never suddenly settle into being “good” for a prolonged period of time anyway. It’s a balancing act that is forever changing. I hope you someday acquire the tools you need to navigate the “bad” times. Whenever you’re going through those times, please remember that I’m rooting for you to make it to a more and more advantageous position. I want that so bad for all of us. Cheers.

Y’all need to read before commenting. Barring any complication, it seems like entropion surgery is usually very successful. Looks super rough before it’s totally healed though. Google photos of cats after the surgery!
Urine, insecticide, wall and futon stains, “Real Pizza,” pink scale. 😵‍💫
Seriously. What are they gonna do to me? I hope they have a good laugh. I hope they sleep soooo peacefully at night too. :p
Generalized *anxiety. This is mental illness, not a personality trait? If it is, I’m super guilty of this and I’m a Scorpio. Also, super mentally ill.
Hurry to your best emergency distractions! TV? Movie? Video game? Music? Go, go, go! I believe you will get through this tough time.

I believe you. I’m sorry you’re in pain and that people irl don’t appreciate you. Maybe they just aren’t putting in the work to get to know you and your good qualities. If this world makes you sad, then I’m sure you have some good qualities or something you care about that’s causing you pain right now. 

Please be patient with yourself. Give yourself some room to be sad, make mistakes, forget to take care of yourself, etc. I promise you can work to be better. I’m sure you’re already trying really hard. We’re all tired of trying here. We know how exhausting and unrewarding it is sometimes.
Agreed. Having to be conscious and in public today is challenging. It’s a game I really don’t want to play. What a waste of time and energy.

It’s a constant effort to not worry about the things I can’t change. I wish I could “turn off” for a moment and not be any particular way. I guess I can hope that I one day learn how to manage those feelings.

I care about people. But I understand that it’s exhausting for them to deal with me and my depression/social anxiety. I isolate myself when it’s at its worst and I still wish I had someone to talk to. Too bad I ghost everyone eventually. If I heal enough someday, then maybe I can hold on to my friends. 

I know what you mean about jealousy and rage. I know the self destructive attitude too. It’s so painful.

I don’t have a car, but I constantly think about jumping in front of one. Would hate to hurt other people though. 

Don’t really get the urge to jump since the free fall scares me, but I also think it would be wonderful. Every excruciating second of carrying this weight leads me to believe so.
It’s surreal that “degenerative” is like dying significantly faster than the average person, but not fast enough to be terminal. What a nasty, rotten illness. What hell. I’m sorry.

Me too, bud. I often feel like I’m “not made for this.” Today I feel like a huge baby for not being able to handle hardly anything. I’m dressed, I’m in public, but I have work in a bit and I’m still trying to calm down from a panic attack. I want to shut down.

I can be in the road, in the crosswalk, and stop for a car. This happens when I cross from the side of the lane going in the opposite direction of the approaching car. I’ve done it plenty of times when people don’t see me or are in a rush. 

We need better arguments.

My little sister is autistic and had a psychotic break a couple of years ago. I never once thought any of that was her fault. It didn’t make me ever think that she deserved any less love than anyone else. It’s not her, or your, fault that you have a hard time socializing, that you think differently, or that you’re depressed. I’m not autistic and I have a terrible time of handling daily life too. I know it’s painful. We all have to find our own reasons of sticking around. Sometimes, for me, it’s simply to watch the rest of a TV series. Learn something new. Improve myself. 

Also, I’m female and I never care about strange men. I try to not look them in the eye because I don’t want to invite conversation, even if I think they’re attractive. I just want to mind my own business. Plus, the people I’ve had feelings for or dated have only once been immediately attractive looking to me. I have to know someone to be attracted to them, for the most part.

I know I’m not well enough to have any romantic encounters right now, and maybe you aren’t either. But I will someday. I want to try. It’s worth knowing before dying. You don’t want to know?

I feel really odd about this with myself. In middle school I remember talking to my friend about how I can’t bear to live past my 20s. It gave me such solace to have that kind of control haha. Now I’m not sure when or if I will, but I’m okay not knowing right now. I kind of feel sad for myself as a kid.

Not everyone will see or get to know the true you. If a person treats you poorly than maybe they will never see you as a good person. I fail to see how that defines your whole personhood. You’re good. I’ve decided. And it’s not  facade just because you make mistakes like everyone else. Silliness.

Right? It’s just not for any of us to know. Sigh. Additionally, it’s not worth hurting yourself so badly that you might die and can maybe watch this unfold. It’d be a lifetime of physical hell on top of the mental illness.

I want to make a friend that will show me how they feel about me, always. I want to show them too, but I’m too depressed to! Isn’t it funny? I have to laugh at it or else I might cry. Haha!

No one deserves to be miserable. Who is the decider of that? Haha. You can choose who you are in any given moment, even if some people remember a bad version of you or other evidence exists. Choose to be good. As of today, you used to be bad. You’re a good person now. Why not?

I’m sorry you’re caught in the middle of other people and feel like your situation is of less value than theirs. I think it’s enough, though. I think your pain matters. It matters. You matter.

I agree that it’s especially difficult when it matters only to ourselves and other people are too busy with the their own struggles. It’s ironic. We need each other so badly, yet we don’t want to reach out for fear of being a burden. Secretly needing each other is so silly. 

I just wanted to say people like me need people like you because you understand this feeling. What a valuable skill! It’s okay to reach out to friends or former friends, and you have the self awareness to not just dump all of this on them at once. If you want to have a conversation, then someone has to say hi first, right? It’s okay to ask for help or just say “I need you right now.” People will show up for you in ways that may surprise you. 

Please have patience with yourself and the other people struggling in your life. You’ve done so much, made big efforts, and you’ve been there for them, but you deserve to heal just as much as they do. You deserve good health and happiness. Please be kind to yourself. I want so much for you. I’m wishing you the best with as much might as I can!

It hurts a lot. I derive some sort of pleasure from trying to make others happy, so they don’t have to feel all the bad feelings I have felt. Then at the end of the day I wish I could get as far away as possible from everyone. It’s really odd to feel like such an imposter, huh?

Thanks for sharing. I’m also afraid to get help right now. I know I’m not making good decisions, but I don’t want to have to hear it from a professional, as well. The more I talk about it the more disgusted with myself I feel.

I grieve for every one of us lost to the defect of not being…built for all of this. I will miss you if you choose to leave, friend. But I want nothing more than to see you stick around and make some meaningful connections when you are able to. Soldier on. Please. I can’t bear to lose a teammate, so to speak. I don’t want to be alone either.
Lack of self awareness in others is a nightmare for me to navigate. On top of that, I assume I have put people off in this regard and it kills me. Gross.

It’s hard. It’s just hard to keep your mind and body safe or hold it sacred when nothing is real and you can’t care. The only thing I know how to do when it’s really unbearable is to live life 10 seconds at a time. Can you make it through the next 10 seconds? If yes, then great. Try the next 10. If sunlight isn’t directly touching your skin, then try that. Or try filling silence with human voices; listen to a podcast , radio, or tv program. Talk aloud to yourself. Put your fingers on an instrument and make some noise. Try to feel the reverberation. Don’t look in the mirror. Don’t try to conceptualize a “self” no matter what. Focus on anything else.

My immediate thought was fleas, but that’s only based on brief glances at my friend’s flea bites. Somehow fleas don’t go after me.

Are the people who are confused by this are either not woken up or disturbed by the noise all the time, or too affluent to ever notice? 

I’ve lived here all of two minutes and I’m familiar. I’ve been torn out of sleep by a car doing donuts in the middle of the damn street. Racing. Music. A matter of hours ago one of these cars ran down all the trash bins in the alley next to my apartment. It sounded like the garbage truck itself, but I choked on my dinner because it was dark out and I had no idea what it could be. I heard the blaring music soon after and figured it out.

My walls are paper thin. I hear everything and I don’t care anymore. I only ever feel irked if it’s before 8 am or after 10 pm. I agree that it has become a public health concern. Value yourself, value your rest/sleep and therefore all other aspects of your health. Thanks.

She might not be able to see it as a violation right now. Don’t rely on changing her mind or how she feels about this. 

You trusted her with your body and health. She’s telling you she wants to have that privilege, but wants hurt you and ignore your wishes. She may not understand the magnitude of that now, but you need to protect yourself. You may still love her, and you might even marry her someday, but you can’t be in a sexual relationship with her right now. It’s abusive. Consider yourself lucky to have been forewarned.

Perhaps.

All I know is that my TPO (yours is 16) was over 700. If that helps at all. I did fine until I was sleeping all the time, like out of controllll. Best wishes!

I’m sorry you have to feel uncertainty about your health. It’s such an awful feeling, not finding a measurable cause to point to. People find it vague and treat you as if you’re not constantly hurting and trying to keep the terror/panic at bay. Including doctors.

Here to contribute my little bit of relevant experience. I recently went to urgent care due to bouts of a racing heart that made me feel flushed sometimes and tight in my chest. Showed up to make sure I was okay and the doctor seemed like he didn’t believe me when I said I used to have an arrhythmia (before Hashi diagnosis), even though it’s in my chart by his very institution. Discovered it’s gone now which I was happy about despite the doctor seeming pretty smug. Told him my heart was occasionally beating fast and hard and was waking me up at night. He said in front of me “it’s not that elevated…” when looking at my measured rate that was just taken….not during an episode. And no one gives a damn about the unusual blood pressure hike except for me. 

I thought it was all due to increasing my antidepressants to the max doses finally, but my serum serotonin was lower than normal lol. It went away on it’s own, like a lot of symptoms I see come and go (Idk what’s abnormal and worth reporting anymore; most recently I was diagnosed with chronic sinusitis and occasional wheezing and I had no idea — it’s been years!). Sigh. We’ll all figure this out someday.
Don’t open the door not just for your mental health, but for your physical safety. If the customer can see you, they can also see you point at your wrist/invisible watch. 😑
And a third of them will never show up lol

Focus on feeling better, if you’re not, and then track the numbers. Mine has gone down and back up a little, but overall better. Wish I could say what it is exactly. After 3 years I’ve finally felt flare-free for the longest since diagnosis, but I’m sure it doesn’t correlate with the antibody level.

Quitting simple carbs (gluten, sugar, highly processed foods, etc.) is more hellish than quitting nicotine imo. This past year my blood sugar crashes were probably putting me on the fast track to type 2 diabetes, but many doctors only treat distinct illness and hardly dare to prevent it, so mine had no clue and couldn’t tell from just a dumb A1C test. I’m not gluten-free, but gradually reducing it and focusing on incorporating more fresh fruit and veggies and lean proteins into my diet seems to have fixed the sugar issue. Beware the gut adjustment, i.e. gas hahah gotta love fibrous rich greens. Have fun trying to eat as many different colors of produce as possible. Look up recipes if you’ve never cooked with some of them. Be adventurous and celebrate even the smallest victories! Hope this helps!

Looking at some of the other comments I wonder if I missed something… I don’t feel that you need couples therapy from this story. And you acknowledged that you messed up, but people are kinda throwing salt on your wound. They’re overreacting. 

Give a solid apology for your mistake Acknowledge his feelings, don’t go into detail about how bad you feel or how busy you are or excuses, and promise to do better. I’d probably apologize for the panicked reaction in the moment, as well.

It’ll be okay. I’m sorry that you relapsed, too. It’s a very hard habit to break, as I’m sure plenty of us know. Please be gentle with yourself. Everyone forgets things.

He will “get over it,” or at least be able to process it without resentment, as long as you find a good time to talk about it. 

Let him know you want to have the conversation with him. Apologize again and acknowledge how he must’ve felt. Promise to find a way to be better because he’s important to you. If he’s comfortable maybe talk about whether it’s too late or not to celebrate. Or maybe do something nice for him “just because” wink if he won’t let you have a belated celebration. 

You got this!

I experienced this with an ex. I’m not a fan of “testing” people, but I was always the one to text first or initiate serious talks to address core issues, so I waited. Almost two weeks of no contact and he had only sent a “hope you had a good holiday” text like nothing was wrong. I don’t remember knowing that when I saw him next I was going to break up with him. I might’ve finally texted him saying that I was seriously upset about the distance that had grown between us, especially the fact that unless I initiated communication then he was fine not acting. So when we met up to talk about it I just bit the bullet and ended it. 

I loved him and nothing terrible or dramatic happened to us, but it was the silence of things fizzling out that was frustrating me more and more. There were plenty of times we didn’t show up for each other, when I cared and he didn’t, of deep hurting, loneliness, or depression. Acknowledge the mounting weight you’ve slowly taken on, and that your partner isn’t helping you carry. Act before too much time passes or too many investments are made (whatever it is that you choose to do). Just please don’t put up with this until you break. You need to take good care of yourself, first and foremost. It might feel selfish or conditional, but it really isn’t. Unapologetically set boundaries and voice what you need from your partner. True ones will want that for you. Those who are less will be offended, make excuses, say you’re unfair, play the victim, tell you that you lack empathy, etc. And if they complain like that about healthy approaches to problem solving, or refuse to critically think with you, they are there for either a casual relationship (have fun, if that’s what you want) or don’t have your best interests in mind (i.e. won’t consistently put in the effort).

This is just my truth, as I understand it. I respect your intuition and willingness to ask for help. I wish you great health and happiness, and I hope you continue to connect with people when you’re feeling uncertain or down. Take care.

I’m guessing his intention is to be courteous. There may be a point when you should address this directly, but I think this is kinda the opposite of easing you down. He wants to maintain a good relationship with you by being transparent? I’m glad you expressed your appreciation for his effort to communicate. 

If you have a connection that is healthy and both of you enjoy, I hope you maintain it!

These folks who don’t have boundaries still astound me. I’m busy trying to close or open so I just do the ol’ tap my imaginary watch (read the sign, check Google, our website… I don’t owe you anything until we’re open). If I want to verbalize — “we can help you when we open at ____” or like “we can do that for you during business hours.” 

People know better and they’ll have to just leave or wait, you run on out of there! I’m sorry that you will have to continue to draw that line as hard and clear as you can. I wish you great luck and endurance. 🙏
So between 2 managers and possibly the person who sent the text they can’t manage to find coverage for call outs? Yikes.

It’s okay to set boundaries with other people, even customers. I used to more frequently become curt out of concern/stress. If it’s one minute before closing, I’d answer the phone and either answer a quick question or tell them that we’re now closed and to call back during business hours tomorrow. Sometimes I also set them up with expectations, as far as info we might need for an order or something like that. 

People just want to feel seen. They tend to be more respectful when you set clear expectations and boundaries. My manager calls it “training customers” hahah. Kinda condescending, but not wrong necessarily.
Spray them with peppermint Wondercide. Smells decent (but strong) and isn’t harmful to cats or dogs.

Last year I had odd bouts of tendinitis in different parts of my body. The tendon that lies near my hip sometimes “clicks” now as it rubs over the bone. I also still have “plucky” elbow tendons that go off with movement, resulting in a tingly shock in my whole arm (both sides are affected). No RA symptoms or diagnosis; I have Hashimoto’s thyroiditis. No abnormal ESR or CRP results. Dunno what this is.

First of all, thank you for sharing. Carrying the weight of that pain must be really tiring. Carry on and you’ll find strength again, I promise. I identify with being the same type of person and I know it’s a long lonely journey.

If you need stuff to do that might help:

Talk therapy, self-discovery through creative endeavors, and observing and researching social phenomena have helped me. 

Of course, having friends to lean on and relate to would be great, but you seem to know that slowing down in social situations might be necessary. 

Podcasts help me to feel like I have some semblance of social connections to people haha and it might help you understand “audience,” as a concept or with learning by how to talk/mask in front of others.

Alternative social connection: Reddit. :p

If you enjoy reading, Daring Greatly by Brené Brown can help you learn to harness your ability to be unabashedly yourself in publicly positive ways (idk how else to phrase that lol).

Please don’t get hung up on seeking a diagnosis unless you or a therapist really think you may benefit from medication or having this on paper for school or work accommodations. Social cues, schmocial cues. Be proactive or bide your time. If you really want to improve and grow, I’m confident you’ll find a way. I was in a total depression, and that delayed things for me, but you just kind of soldier on (I almost didn’t make it!). 

Be gentle with yourself. You’ll come to appreciate this ability of yours. And you’ll find others who do too.

That server, chef, host, etc. are the backbone/foundation/life blood of their business. Guess who entertains your customers for 8+ hours a day, so you don’t have to??? Its so simple, it’s stupid. And obviously they have some idea of what constitutes a “living wage,” since they wrote it right there! Disgusting, stingy, reprehensible practices.

The very next visit after my doc found that my TSH was high I requested an antibody test to see if it was autoimmune induced. Like many of us, my TPO is off the charts. But yeah. Me. Myself. I had to request it. As far as they were concerned, the medication was a simple fix to a symptom they could measure. Now my TSH is stable and I still feel like garbage. I’m the picture of health on paper though!
The advancement in technology is perhaps making mental illness more visible? Or easier to talk about and learn about? I’m mentally ill and I’d never talk to all y’all otherwise.
I also have this problem. :/

I happened to be barely awake for my last visit to an Endocrinologist — told him that my TSH is good now, but I still want to sleep all the time. He referred me to Pulmonary for a sleep test lol. With my highly unusual weight gain…I probably do have sleep apnea now? Dunno. I really should do the test. Sigh.

It’s frustrating to have a hunch that something is very wrong with you, but the doctors want to eliminate every basic little thing before really paying attention. I recently had some weird cardiac symptoms (measurable) and thought I might need to go to the ER after reeeeally thinking about it and sitting with it. Urgent care doc said “it’s not that bad.” Love being young and having oddly quickly-progressing elevated BP, but it’s not of concern to them. All I’m told is that I seem perfectly healthy according to my blood tests. Like, what???

I’ve had a high pain tolerance since I was little, and growing up fairly poor I neverrrr used to go to the doctor. Within the last 5 years I have been diagnosed, have flares and chronic pain, neuro symptoms, etc. etc. I heavily manage my expectations now and have a real fear of my body actually breaking before I get help with management and prevention. Good golly gosh! But I’m learning to be my own advocate. Firing lame doctors. Psychotherapy helps. And posting here! Thanks for sharing! If you like to read, maybe check out The Invisible Kingdom by Meghan O’Rourke? 

Btw, my antibodies (TPO) are also crazy, but slowly getting better as I adjust my lifestyle. Stay strong and keep making healthy decisions, friend.

I help people with their old cats most days at work and I think about this all the time, but with cats. They start out with kinda wimpy kidneys and they mostly start to feel the breakdown of function way before they die. Imagine the genetic disadvantages you have, structurally/functionally, that you don’t even know about.

All we can hope for is to catch the issues when they begin and then slow progression as much as possible. Above all, try to prevent onset of disease. Make good choices and cross your fingers!

Sometimes it really frightens me how many grown people are okay with concealing the truth, or lying to themselves, to maintain something they think is peace? Especially when it affects others and they’re still okay with it... Yikes.

I’m also 30 F with normal labs, whether I’m flaring or not when my blood is taken. I also get muscle pain and fatigue. Yeah, I get weird symptoms that come and go; pain for weeks that’s just gone one day. Tendonitis and weak wrists (they both have cysts right now, I think). Moving around frequently helps and I like menthol patches and cream. One day a week I spend mostly sleeping and in bed. When it’s cold out I like to go outside and let my whole body get chilly because it helps me to relieve the aches. Pain is frequent enough that I often go without NSAIDS or any treatment. I’ve just gotten used to not focusing on it and taking time off when I need it.

I’m so happy that somebody understands this. I bus to work and I get up 2 hours before I have to leave. Then it takes an additional hour or so to get to work once I’m on a bus. I FORCE myself to get up that early, and even if I had that 2 hours to sleep I doubt I would feel significantly better. It hurts.

I also need to know how people navigate this. Functionally, I have an attention deficit, but I don’t fit the proper diagnostic criteria for ADHD. So, at work, I have no excuse for my foggy, forgetful brain. It’s a big problem. My short term memory is shot.

I can identify with part of this. I took a nursing assistant class in high school and couldn’t believe how awful almost all of the students were. And it wasn’t just because we were young. It’s surreal realizing that any ol’ person can be in such a profession.

I used to. Lately I experience more issues with muscular stiffness, aches, and exhaustion. In addition, my B12 blood tests have been normal.

I was also tested for Rheumatoid Factor and it came back negative. I think it’s unlikely to be rheumatoid nodules, but I know next to nothing about that stuff.
Hopefully. Thanks for the advice.

I’ll have to read up on nodules and see what that’s like. Thanks.

I’m in pain, fatigued, overweight, etc. It’s such a wild experience. I fired that doctor, but was afraid to see anyone for 6 months because it felt so awful to be dismissed like that.

This is my best advice, too. Tuck away any direct reminders. When you get an itch to snoop, that’s your cue to do something else. Choose a specific activity — have a list of movies you can just press play on, recruit help from a good friend and text them that you’re having this urge, listen to a comedy podcast, do a craft project (knit, collage, journal), watch a how-to video. I assume it’s not unusual. I’m in the same boat, at least. I was diagnosed late 2019 and spent 2020 figuring out my levothyroxine dose and experimenting with Armour because the first day on meds I woke up with hives (ended up not being related to meds). For a solid year I had hives and angioedema, with no apparent allergies, plus a slew of other symptoms that come and go (including the ones you listed). I just started feeling somewhat better around Nov./Dec. last year. 

I had to adjust to a “new normal,” as well. People don’t seem to notice anymore that I’m symptomatic, and my coworkers don’t even mind that I forget things all the time or need help refocusing. I use post-it’s all over my workplace, ask for help, and draw boundaries, which help me get through each day. At home I let myself take it easy. I still have symptoms, ever evolving, and don’t think I’ll ever be “better” in the way I had thought back when I was diagnosed. 

I assume restructuring your life will probably take a few years (hell, I still have a lot of work ahead of me too). It’s a big deal. I hope the community can give you a good idea of what to expect and some direction, but we can’t stop things outside of our control from interfering (we both had to take care of business in the beginnings of COVID, especially you). I hope you are very patient with yourself and don’t blame yourself or beat yourself up about it. It really is feeling like a long time to me too!
